doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Reflecting on a career of writing music
summary: He feels blessed to write for a living, from a one-musician town.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well this has really been interesting to hear from the side of the guy who puts it all down on paper. I really appreciate you joining me. And I look at this list of people you’ve written for, it’s like a legacy. I think putting music down on paper is really a great thing to leave, not just the recordings of it.

Yeah it’s always going to be there, but a lot of those people are gone. It’s probably never going to be performed again but I really feel blessed in being able to do that for a living. How much better does it get? I sit there at my piano thinking this is what I do for a living.
From a guy from a town that had one musician of questionable character.
